exposure: BMI category (normal 18.5-24.9, overweight 25.0-29.9, obese 30.0-39.9, and morbidly obese 40 or greater)
outcome: Prolonged incision-to-delivery interval (defined as 90th percentile or greater of the study population or 18 minutes or longer)
cohort: 21,372 women with singleton gestations undergoing uncomplicated primary and repeat cesarean deliveries from the Maternal-Fetal Medicine Units Network Cesarean Registry.
finding: Increasing BMI is related to increased incision-to-delivery interval and total operative time at cesarean delivery.
mod_finding: Morbidly obese BMI exposes women to the highest risk of prolonged incision-to-delivery interval.
